title: RWB-S9-E7012-APP: the fee-approval path has no published operation, no approval column or list value, no rule row and no fee-schedule entity
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.3 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E7012-APP; context pack S9 rwb-partner (service row, ownership rows, Architecture v5 slides 2, 4, 5 and 8); legacy RWB-E7-012; FSD S9 Partner management v4 A1.2, A2.9, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S9 Partner management v3 T0 to T6.1 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-28, R-UNI-39, R-WO-37, R-DIS-54, R-LIT-41 and R-LIT-42; LDM and Data Dictionary v8 partner, partner_instruction and LOV-REF-TABLE; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21; Program BRD v4 REQ-S9-001 and REQ-S9-004
description: (1) No operation of the Ownership Map approves a partner fee: the six operations of S9 are GET /partners (API-S9-001), POST /cases/{caseId}/instructions (API-S9-002), GET /partner/instructions (API-S9-003), POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/accept (API-S9-004), POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/results (API-S9-005) and POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/invoices (API-S9-006), and none of them is an approval, while the legacy story's own endpoint table lists only the instruction read and the result submission. (2) No column and no list value carries an approved fee: partner_instruction has nine fields (DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016) and LOV-INSTR-STATUS has six values (SENT, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, IN_PROGRESS, DONE, RECALLED), none of which is an approval, an approver or an approved instant. (3) No rule row names the condition: the Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 has no partner or fee rule set, and the nearest rows are R-UNI-28 (stop fee payments on insolvency), R-WO-37 (calculate the agency fee), R-DIS-54 (match the vendor fee) and R-LIT-41 and R-LIT-42 (legal spend approval), none of which is a partner-fee approval. (4) The fee schedule that FEAT-PRM-02 keeps as versioned reference data has no entity in the LDM v8 and no code in LOV-REF-TABLE, so the rate, the basis and the version the claim is judged on cannot be cited. (5) No event carries an approval: the two events of S9 are EV-20 InstructionIssued and EV-21 PartnerResultSubmitted. (6) The plan's C and X rows are empty although TSD S9 T5.2.2 declares the rwb-document upload link class C and the partner gateway class X. (7) FSD S9 A2.9.3.3 names the Finance and CFO delegate as also using, and TSD S9 T6.1 carries no such role.
evidence: Context pack S9 ownership rows: three tables, six REST operations, two events, no job and one workflow; TSD S9 T-A.1 API-S9-001 to API-S9-006 and T5.2.2; TSD S9 T3.1 DF-PRT-008 to DF-PRT-016 and T3.2 LOV-INSTR-STATUS; LDM v8 partner_instruction and LOV-REF-TABLE (no fee code); Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-28, R-UNI-39, R-WO-37, R-DIS-54, R-LIT-41 and R-LIT-42; FSD S9 A2.9.3.3 and Screens; legacy RWB-E7-012 Endpoints, Data and Permission checks
area: API contract, data model, business rules, reference data, events, access
owner_role: Solution architect with the API owner, the rwb-case reference-data owner, the rwb-decision rule owner and the rwb-access owner
proposed: Publish the approval operation on the partner base (for example POST /partner/instructions/{instructionId}/fee-approval) in the API Specification and the Ownership Map, or name the operation that already carries it; decide whether an approved fee is a new column, a new list value or the decision record only, and raise the DB story if a column is needed; publish one rule row for the partner-fee check with its own ID and its schedule version; add the fee-schedule entity or reference-table code to FEAT-PRM-02 and the LDM; add the Finance and CFO delegate to TSD S9 T6.1 or correct FSD S9 A2.9.3.3; and settle whether an approved fee reaches rwb-payment and rwb-reporting on an event or on a read.

title: RWB-S9-E7012-CON: the approval operation, the approval-entry attributes, the fee-schedule read, the three consumed rows and the delegate right have no published baseline
source: Template and Rules v1 R5.4, R5.5, R7.2 and R9; split plan slice RWB-S9-E7012-CON; context pack S9 rwb-partner; legacy RWB-E7-012; FSD S9 Partner management v4 A2.9, Requirements served and Screens; TSD S9 Partner management v3 T0.1 to T0.3, T2, T3.0 to T3.3, T4, T5.2, T5.3, T6.1 and T-A; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-28, R-UNI-39 and R-WO-37; LDM and Data Dictionary v8 partner, partner_instruction and LOV-REF-TABLE; Recovery Workbench API Specification v4 base /api/recovery/partner/v1; Event and Messaging Design v4 EV-20 and EV-21
description: (1) The act of approving a partner fee has no published operation, and the read of an approved claim has none either, so the contract baseline declares both as placeholders; a screen act must be served by a REST operation on the partner base and the Ownership Map gives the service exactly six, all of them the panel, instruction, result or invoice story's. (2) The approval-entry attributes have no schema of their own: the local record of DP-03 is a library object and no source fixes the claim, the schedule version, the compared amount or the approver attribute, so the baseline proposes them and the library owner confirms. (3) The fee schedule has no entity in the LDM v8 and no code in LOV-REF-TABLE, so the reference-data read, its version token and its operation name carry a placeholder and its owner is fixed only by the R3 default ruling. (4) TSD S9 T5.2.2 declares two consumed contracts, the P5 upload link as class C and the partner gateway as class X, and the plan's C and X rows are both empty. (5) The finance delegate of FSD S9 A2.9.3.3 has no row in TSD S9 T6.1, so the baseline records a conflict rather than declaring a right. (6) TSD S9 T4 says the module acts on events from P3, while T5.2.2 records no event consumed, so the baseline follows the contract table and records the disagreement. (7) No event of the service carries a fee approval, so an approved fee reaches no other service on the event catalogue.
evidence: Context pack S9 ownership rows (six REST operations, two events, no job); TSD S9 T-A.1, T5.2.2, T5.2.3, T3.1, T3.2 and T6.1; TSD S9 T4 against T5.2.2; LDM v8 partner_instruction, partner and LOV-REF-TABLE; FSD S9 A2.9.3.3 and Screens; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-UNI-28 and R-UNI-39; legacy RWB-E7-012 Endpoints, Permission checks and Validation and messages
area: API contract, data model, reference data, access, events
owner_role: Solution architect with the API owner, the platform library owner, the rwb-case reference-data owner and the rwb-access owner
proposed: Publish the approval operation and the decided-claim read on the partner base with their rights and their error set; confirm the approval-entry attributes against the local record schema; publish the fee-schedule entity or its reference-table code with its version and its read operation; add the rwb-document upload link and the partner gateway to the plan's C and X rows; resolve the Finance and CFO delegate in TSD S9 T6.1 rather than in a contract; settle whether TSD S9 T4's P3 subscription exists and publish the consumed event if it does; and decide how an approved fee reaches rwb-payment and rwb-reporting.
